html:
The Lickanantay, or Atacameño, are an Indigenous people of the Atacama Desert of northern Chile, around the oases of San Pedro de Atacama and the Loa River, and nearby parts of Argentina.

They farmed maize, quinoa and potatoes with irrigation in the oases, herded llamas and ran caravans across the desert and the Andes. Their culture took ideas from Tiwanaku around 500 to 1000, and in the late 1400s the Inca brought them into their empire. Their own language, Kunza, died out in the 1900s. Their neighbours included the Aymara to the north, the Diaguita to the south and the Chango fishers on the coast. Today the lithium and copper mines of the Salar de Atacama, on their land, are a major issue for them.
sum: The Lickanantay, or Atacameño, are an Indigenous people of the Atacama Desert of northern Chile, around the oases of San Pedro de Atacama and the Loa River, and nearby parts of Argentina.
